questions.stem: All of the following are features of DNA replication, EXCEPT:SemiconservativeSemi-discontinuousTemplate IndependentRequires RNA primerUnidirectionalSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
3, and 5 are correct

Features of DNA replication:

  • Semi-conservative (newly synthesized DNA has one strand from template DNA and the other is newly synthesized)
  • Template-dependent (DNA replication requires a template.)
  • Begins at origin(s) of replication
  • Requires RNA primer
  • The direction of synthesis is always 5’ to 3’
  • Bi-directional
  • Semi-discontinuous (leading strand – continuous; a lagging strand – discontinuous)



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd edition Page No. 352

questions.stem: True about telomerase:It is a ribonucleoproteinHas reverse transcriptase activityRNA containing ribozymeActive only in cancer cellsElongates the G-rich strand of telomeric DNASelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1, 2, and 5 are correct

Telomerase:

  • Has its own RNA template
  • It’s a ribonucleoprotein
  • Elongates the G-rich strand of telomeric DNA using its own RNA as a template.
  • The replicative potential of cancer cells and germ cells is due to telomerase
  • Contains RNA, but is not a ribozyme since the catalytic activity is due to the protein part, not the RNA part.
  • Prevents telomere shortening (prevents aging or senescence)

Activity of telomerase enzyme

  • decreased in aging
  • increased in cancer

Premature aging (Progeria) occurs if telomerase decreases

questions.stem: An experiment was conducted with rats in which they were fed nitrate-rich food for several days. The DNA analysis of intestinal cells showed a lot of deaminated cytosine. The most probable reason for this finding is a defect in which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Base Excision Repair
  • The presence of deaminated bases is due to defective base excision repair which corrects for abnormal bases such as uracil, hypoxanthine, and xanthine formed by spontaneous deamination of original bases cytosine, adenine, and guanine respectively.

Enzymes involved in Base excision repair are as:

  • DNA glycosylases
  • AP endonucleases
  • DNA polymerase I
  • DNA ligase
  • The defect in this repair system causes MUTYH-associated polyposis in humans, which is a rare disease.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 380

questions.stem: On colonoscopy examination of a 40-year-old man, he was found to have right-sided, mucinous colon cancer, with no other lesions or polyps seen. He has a family history of colon cancers and ovarian cancers. He most probably has a defect in which of the following processes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mismatch repair
  • The patient has Hereditary Nonpolyposis Colorectal Cancer (HNPCC), which is due to specific mutations in proteins involved in mismatch repair and is primarily right-sided with the absence of any polyps.
  • It occurs due to mutations in any of seven different genes involved in mismatch repair (which is distinct from the generalized DNA repair system, mutations which lead to xeroderma pigmentosum).
  • These genes are all tumor suppressor genes.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 380

questions.stem: The two strands of DNA have to separate for the replication machinery to work on single strands of DNA. The unwinding of DNA causes the creation of supercoils which are relieved by the action of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Topoisomerase
  • During the unwinding of DNA, relief of supercoil is made possible by Topoisomerase
  • DNA helicase unwinds the DNA without cutting but using energy from the hydrolysis of ATP.
  • Gyrase is a bacterial type II topoisomerase that acts on closed circular DNA (bacteria have circular DNA).

Extra Information:

Linking number

  • Number of times one strand of DNA has to be passed through the other strand to separate both the strands completely.
  • Its an integer for a closed circular DNA.
  • Topoisomers are DNA forms that differ in their linking number.
  • Topoisomerases are the enzymes that can change the linking number of DNA.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl is brought to the dermatologist by her parents. She has many freckles on her face, neck, arms, and hands and her parents report that she is highly sensitive to sunlight. On examination, two basal cell carcinomas are observed on her face. The process which is most likely defective in this patient is?

options.label: B
options.text: Removal of mismatched bases from the 3’ end of Okazaki fragments

options.label: C
options.text: Removal of pyrimidine dimers from DNA

questions.answerText: Removal of pyrimidine dimers from DNA
questions.solutionHtml:
Removal of pyrimidine dimers from DNA
  • The patient is showing characteristics of a condition known as Xeroderma pigmentosum. These individuals have sensitivity to sunlight with extensive freckling on parts of the body exposed to the sun. They are also prone to developing skin cancer at a young age.

questions.stem: A 17-month-old girl suffered from recurring respiratory infections. Injection of Diphtheria-Pertussis-Tetanus (DPT) and Typhoid vaccine produced only a minimal response. The lysate of the girl's erythrocytes was found to lack detectable adenosine deaminase activity. Her mother and father both showed approximately 50% of the normal red cell adenosine deaminase activity. Diagnose the disease.
questions.solutionHtml:
SCID

SCID (Severe combined immunodeficiency)

  • SCID occurs due to a deficiency of the enzyme ADA which converts adenosine to inosine (and deoxyadenosine to deoxyinosine).
  • In the absence of this enzyme, an accumulation of deoxyadenosine occurs. Deoxyadenosine is toxic and will accumulate in the blood cells, eventually forming dATP through salvage reactions.
  • The dATP will, in part, inhibit ribonucleotide reductase, and the cells with high dATP levels will not be able to proliferate when signaled to do so due to the lack of deoxyribonucleotide precursors leading to a lack of DNA synthesis in immune cell precursors.
  • In SCID, the thymus is virtually absent, and there is virtually no T- cell, and B-cell production.

Regarding other options:

Hypokalemia

●        Reduction in cells potassium ions and their replacement with protons from the blood causing alkalosis

Crushing Muscular Trauma

●        Muscle cell damage resulting from pressure or crushing.

Lesch–Nyhan syndrome

●        Deficiency of Hypoxanthine Guanine Phospho Ribosyl Transferase (HGPRT).

●        The main clinical features are Hyperuricemia and Self-mutilation

questions.stem: In prokaryotic DNA replication enzyme DNA Gyrase help in the unwinding of DNA before replication can begin. This enzyme is an equivalent of which of the following enzymes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prokaryotic DNA Topoisomerase II

DNA Gyrase:

  • Counterpart of Topoisomerase II in prokaryotes.
  • Introduces negative supercoils (underwinding is known as negative supercoiling) and
  • Uses ATP

Topoisomerase I

Topoisomerase II

●        Makes cuts on the single strand

●        Makes cuts on both strands

●        Formation of a covalent DNA-enzyme

●        complex preserves free energy.

●        ATP is not needed.

●        ATP is needed.

●        Relives only negative supercoils in E. coli

●        relives both negative and positive in Eukaryotes.

●        Relaxes both negative & positive supercoils.

●        Positive supercoil is relieved by introducing negative supercoils.

questions.stem: To pack tightly in a cell, double helical DNA is wound around itself one or more times creating either negative or positive supercoils. Supercoiled DNA is found in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Both
  • Supercoiling occurs in both Prokaryotes & Eukaryotes.
  • Supercoiling is because of dsDNA & dsDNA are present in Both Prokaryotes & Eukaryotes.
  • Eukaryotes have closed, circular, dsDNA molecules in their mitochondria, as do plant chloroplasts.
  • A prokaryotic organism typically contains a single, circular, dsDNA molecule.
  • Note: Circular DNA is “supercoiled”, that is, the double helix crosses over on itself one or more times.
  • Supercoiling can result in over-winding (positive supercoiling) or under-winding (negative supercoiling) of DNA.



Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition Page No. 351

questions.stem: The processivity of DNA Polymerase is an expression used to define the number of nucleotides added to the nascent chain before the polymerase disengages from the template. Which is the most processive DNA polymerase?
questions.solutionHtml:
DNA Polymerase III

Processive enzymes are those that remain bound to the end of the growing chain and keep on adding substrates e.g. Glycogen Phosphorylase, DNA polymerases

  • Of all the prokaryotic DNA polymerases, DNA Polymerase III catalyzes the highest rate (20-50 nucleotides/sec) of chain elongation and is the most processive (0.5 Mb/cycle).
  • Of all the eukaryotic polymerases, DNA polymerase δ is the most processive.

questions.stem: A group of researchers while testing an experimental drug discovered a mutant of E.coli which was unable to replicate in the presence of the drug. Later analysis of the mutant strain revealed that there is a defect in removing the RNA primers during the replication. Which of the following enzyme is most likely affected by this drug in this strain?
questions.solutionHtml:
DNA polymerase I
  • DNA polymerases are the main enzymes involved in DNA replication. In prokaryotes such as E. coli, there are three DNA polymerases named DNA polymerase I, II, and III performing different functions.
  • Other enzymes required for replication include helicase, topoisomerases, primase, and ligase. Before polymerization can occur, the two parental DNA strands are unwounded using helicase for cutting and topoisomerases by removing supercoiling.
  • As DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to the exiting chain hence a short RNA primer is synthesized by primase enzyme using DNA as a template. One primer is required for the leading strand, but multiple primers are required for the lagging strand.
  • The leading strand is synthesized continuously in the 5’ → 3’ direction (See Fig.) and it needs only one RNA primer while the lagging strand is synthesized in short stretches in the 5’ → 3’ direction and requires many RNA primers.
  • After the proofreading, DNA polymerase I remove RNA primers by 5’-3’exonuclease activity and fills the gap by synthesizing DNA using 5’-3’ polymerase activity.
  • DNA ligase catalyzes the formation of a phosphodiester bond between DNA synthesized by DNA polymerase III and that formed by DNA polymerase I using energy (ATP).




Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 6th Edition Page No. 374
